subject: Request: temporary KMS handback + short retention evidence for onboarding
messages:
From: Hannah Lewis <hannah@medflux.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary KMS handback + short retention evidence for onboarding

Diego —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. As we begin the security onboarding checklist on our side there are two near-term asks from our compliance team that we need help with to keep the procurement timeline intact:

1) A short-lived CMK "handback" window (no longer than 72 hours) or an equivalent key-wrapping mechanism to allow our key custodian to validate KMS integration during the pilot. We absolutely cannot do permanent escrow; this would be strictly time-boxed.

2) A snapshot of audit logs and a list of retained event types (who/what/when) for the onboarding environment covering the last 30 days — they want to validate log granularity and retention behavior before finalize procurement.

Attached is a short Scope doc (medflux_audit_scope_v1.pdf) that highlights the fields they need. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support the temporary handback path, what approvals are required, and an estimated lead time?

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute triage call with your product/security folks tomorrow morning.

Appreciate it —
Hannah Lewis
Head of Security Programs
MedFlux

(attachment: medflux_audit_scope_v1.pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lewis <hannah@medflux.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary KMS handback + short retention evidence for onboarding

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear ask and the scope doc. Looping in Priyom (infra/product), Marissa (security-compliance), and Jonas (platform) so we can triage quickly.

Quick notes from my side:
- We have an internal precedent for short-lived key wrapping for pilots, but it requires a documented exception and a technical playbook (I attached an evidence matrix to start: evidence_matrix.csv).
- My immediate asks for the group: can we provide a 72-hour handback window that is auditable and revocable? What limitations on exported key material are required by infra?
- On logs: we can export a time-bounded audit dump, but we need to confirm which event types are required (auth, key operations, token issuance, internal system actions). Hannah, can you confirm the exact event fields from the scope doc you need us to include?

Proposed next steps:
1) Priyom & Marissa propose a technical approach and list of gating approvals by EOD tomorrow.
2) If proposal is feasible, I will create the Jira ticket and a short canary test plan.
3) Schedule the 30-minute triage (Hannah, do mornings on Wed/Thu work?).

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

(attachment: evidence_matrix.csv)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Hannah Lewis <hannah@medflux.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary KMS handback + short retention evidence for onboarding

Diego / Hannah —

I reviewed the scope doc and ran a quick feasibility check with infra. Summary proposal:

- Temporary key-handback approach: we can support a time-boxed key wrapping flow where Redwood performs a one-time envelope-wrapping of a generated CMK that MedFlux can verify, with the wrapped key material retained in a short-lived escrow that is programmatically zeroed after 72 hours. This avoids handing over cleartext key material and keeps the control plane auditable.

- Audit exports: we can produce an export that includes: KMS API calls (CreateKey/Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/RotateKey), auth events (token issuance, failed logins), and operator actions (deployments that touch key configs). We cannot export internal ephemeral host-level syslogs; those are out-of-scope for procurement but we can provide examples.

Constraints / gating:
- Need written approval from Product Security and Legal for the short-lived escrow workflow.
- Runbook needs a test plan and canary to validate we zero escrow after the window — I recommend a staged pilot in our dev region.

I created a working Jira: REDWOOD-SUP-4512 and uploaded a brief playbook (kms_handback_playbook.md) to the team Drive folder (link below).

If that direction works for MedFlux, next items are:
1) Draft exception approval (ProductSec + Legal) — Marissa, can you take point?
2) Priyom will draft the canary test and produce a sample audit export for Hannah by EOD Tuesday.
3) Schedule triage to confirm fields and the exact retention window for the exported audit snapshot.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Product Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference

(attachment: kms_handback_playbook.md)
